claim_text: A handicap index is the average of a golfer's best score differentials, multiplied by 0.96.
revised_text: Under the World Handicap System a Handicap Index is the average of the lowest 8 of a player's most recent 20 score differentials; the 0.96 multiplier belonged to the USGA formula that preceded it and no longer applies.
context: Slide 'Calculating your handicap' in the Handicapping module of the demo course, revised: the Handicap Index is the average of the lowest 8 of the most recent 20 score differentials (Rules of Handicapping, Rule 5.2); the former 0.96 'bonus for excellence' was removed when the World Handicap System took effect in 2020.

evidence.narrative: Rules of Handicapping, Rule 5.2: Calculation of a Handicap Index — the average of the lowest 8 Score Differentials of the most recent 20.
USGA: what changed with the World Handicap System in 2020 — the bonus for excellence (0.96) was removed.

note: The slide taught the pre-2020 formula; the revision states the current rule and cites it.

claim_text: The USGA Rules of Golf govern competitive play everywhere.
revised_text: The Rules of Golf are written jointly by the USGA and The R&A; the USGA administers them in the United States and Mexico, and The R&A everywhere else.
context: Slide 'Rules of golf' in the Playing module of the demo course, revised: the Rules of Golf are a joint publication of the USGA and The R&A, administered by the USGA in the United States and Mexico and by The R&A in the rest of the world.

evidence.narrative: The Rules of Golf: jointly written and published by the USGA and The R&A; each governs in its own jurisdiction.

note: 'Everywhere' overreached; the revision names both governing bodies and their jurisdictions.
